set.body:
Promote the existing topology-safe SurfaceSet and SurfaceMorph primitives into a first-class viewer feature for named cortical geometry states such as white, smooth white, pial, midthickness, inflated, and sphere.

Architecture:
- SurfaceAsset/viewer model owns a SurfaceSet (one hemisphere and exact ordered topology) plus a selected geometry presentation, rather than only one SurfaceGeometry.
- Viewer state represents either a stable SurfaceKind or a typed transition from one kind to another with SurfaceMorphFraction; reducer actions select a state or advance a transition without embedding a wall clock in shared code.
- Vertex-domain layers, thresholds, opacity, order, selection, and readouts remain attached to mesh-domain identity and survive every geometry-state change.
- Family construction rejects missing defaults, duplicate kinds, hemisphere/topology mismatch, and transform incompatibility needed for morphing.
- Framing is explicit and stable during morphs; default to union-of-endpoint bounds so inflated/spherical transitions do not cause camera zoom pumping.
- Shared compiler separates immutable topology/index identity from mutable position/normal frames.

Backend/performance:
- JavaFX mutates TriangleMesh point/normal buffers on the FX thread while preserving faces, texture atlas, material, camera, and layer resources.
- Three.js mutates position/normal BufferAttributes in place, marks only those attributes dirty, and refreshes bounds without replacing geometry.
- Raster backend remains the deterministic oracle.
- Geometry transitions upload no indices or color/layer payloads and do not rebuild materials.

Acceptance:
- Exact t=0 and t=1 endpoints; linear midpoint and reverse-path symmetry; stable vertex ids, ordered faces, hemisphere, transform, overlays, thresholds, selection, and readouts.
- Invalid topology/transform combinations fail before rendering.
- Shared JVM/JS reducer/compiler tests cover state selection, interruption/reversal, and deterministic transition fractions.
- Asymmetric real cortical fixtures cover white, pial, inflated, and sphere at 0, .25, .5, .75, and 1 with JavaFX/WebGL images compared to the raster oracle and explicit L/R and orientation checks.
- Performance receipts at 32k and 164k vertices prove one initial index upload, zero layer/color uploads during morph, bounded allocation, and recorded p50/p95 frame/update timings on JavaFX and Chrome.
